text: The Table 2 caption states that one player is prespecified as honest and one as liar, so that when the honest player wins honesty is the best strategy. Without precommit the liar wins for any incorrect guess by the judge, even if the incorrect guess differs for different parts of the game tree; with precommit the liar states their claim in advance and cannot change their story, which makes lying harder. The caption states that with or without precommit the honest player wins more often than a random judge, which the authors read as showing that honesty has an advantage.
title: MNIST debate without precommit: honest player still beats a random judge (Table 2)
